title: hotfix: SLO enforcer regional failover ordering causing double-shed under load
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Fixes a race in the SLO enforcer that could lead to duplicated load-shedding decisions during regional failover. Under high cross-region traffic, simultaneous failover and shedding events could be applied out-of-order causing a single request cohort to be shed twice and triggering unnecessary downstream throttles.

Motivation and context: The SLO enforcer coordinates per-region circuit breakers, backoff, and load-shedding policies. In the incident on 2026-02-18 we observed elevated error budgets in eu-west leading to automated regional failover. While failover was underway, burst traffic to fallback regions coincided with load-shedding evaluation; due to a state-machine ordering bug we recorded and applied both the failover and the transient shed decision independently, which causes double-accounting of shed requests and artificially accelerates further shedding in the fallback region (see linked postmortem).

Reproduction: Added unit and integration test fixtures that reproduce the ordering by simulating: 1) region A triggers failover; 2) region B receives short burst and enters shed path; 3) both transitions happen near-simultaneously. Prior behavior: both events were applied without serializing updates to the region state, producing duplicate shed metrics.

Change summary:
- Serialize state machine transitions for regional failover and load-shedding by adding a per-region transition mutex and a small ordering buffer to ensure events originating from the same failover window are deduplicated.
- Add explicit idempotency keys to shed commands so re-applied commands are recognized and ignored.
- Clamp concurrent shed-to-failover transitions in the enforcer to avoid thrash.
- Add unit tests and an integration test that reproduces the incident sequence under deterministic scheduling.
- Update incident doc with mitigation guidance.

Why this is safe as a hotfix: Changes are localized to the SLO enforcer state machine layer and add serialization/idempotency rather than changing policy thresholds. Tests exercise both normal and degraded code paths. Rollout plan includes staged canary to 10% of control plane nodes before full rollout.

Testing performed:
- Local unit tests: enforcer state machine (new deterministic scheduler), idempotency logic.
- Integration test: simulated regional failover + burst scenario running in CI with deterministic scheduling (added flaky guard).
- Canary: deployed to a subset of control plane hosts in staging and then canaryed to 10% production nodes for 2h; monitored shed rates, error budgets, and tracing to ensure no regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] Repro test added and deterministic
- [x] Unit tests added for transition mutex/idempotency
- [x] Integration test added
- [x] Canary plan documented
- [x] Rollback plan documented

References: Incident doc: docs/incidents/2026-02-18-failover-postmortem.md; Linear: ENG-1893, ENG-1910.

Files changed (high level): Listed in files_changed field. Small snippets included in unit test file show synthetic scheduler seeds used to force ordering.

feat(slo-enforcer): add idempotency key for shed commands
test(slo-enforcer): add deterministic integration test for failover+shed ordering
docs: update incident postmortem with mitigation steps and runbook
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can you explain why a simple compare-and-swap on the state enum wasn't sufficient?

Maya Chen: CAS protected the single-state update but we have concurrent event streams (failover + shed) that try to apply different sequences; mutex+ordering buffer keeps per-region ordering window and dedupes logically identical commands.
Liam O'Connor: Tests look good. Suggest adding a short doc inline comment describing the ordering window constants and tradeoffs.
Maya Chen: Added inline doc and adjusted the default window from 250ms->200ms based on canary observations.
Priya Singh: CI flake seen on the integration test on first run; re-ran with deterministic seed and it passed. Approving pending CI pass.
release_notes: Hotfix: Prevents duplicated load-shedding during regional failover by serializing enforcer transitions and deduplicating shed commands. Low-risk, localized change to enforcer state machine. Backported to release/2026-02 for urgent patch.
test_plan: Unit tests: state_machine_test.go covers ordering and idempotency
Integration: deterministic failover+shed test in CI
Canary: staged rollout to 10% control plane nodes for 2h with monitoring (shed-rate, error-budget, p95 latency)
Rollback: immediate rollback of canary release and re-enable previous enforcer binary if regressions observed
rollback_plan: If canary reveals regressions, revert to previous enforcer image and disable automatic regional failover for affected tenants. Notify on-call and create follow-up ticket to revert or patch mainline.
